learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Developmental EEG.
Apply Developmental EEG to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Background frequency, sleep architecture and normal variants evolve with brain maturation.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Paediatric EEG requires age-specific expectations; patterns normal in infancy may be abnormal in an adult and vice versa.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Essential for paediatric seizure assessment and developmental interpretation.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Adult normative databases applied to children produce systematic false deviations.

quizBank.question: Which statement best captures Developmental EEG?
options: Background frequency, sleep architecture and normal variants evolve with brain maturation.
It provides a stand-alone psychiatric diagnosis
It is unaffected by state and artifact
Its interpretation requires no clinical context
quizBank.explanation: Background frequency, sleep architecture and normal variants evolve with brain maturation.

quizBank.question: What is the safest clinical principle for Developmental EEG?
options: Integrate raw signal quality, state, method and clinical context
Assume a coloured map shows exact anatomy
Treat statistical rarity as proof of disorder
quizBank.explanation: EEG and QEEG interpretation requires converging evidence, technical validity and clinical context.

quizBank.question: Which error is most important to avoid in Developmental EEG?
options: Adult normative databases applied to children produce systematic false deviations.
quizBank.explanation: Adult normative databases applied to children produce systematic false deviations.

reviewPrompts.answer: Paediatric EEG requires age-specific expectations; patterns normal in infancy may be abnormal in an adult and vice versa.
Essential for paediatric seizure assessment and developmental interpretation.
Adult normative databases applied to children produce systematic false deviations.
Development is not noise—it is the reference frame.
